This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. The “Learn more” button above demonstrates smooth transitions and proper visual feedback.

Try using the Tab key to navigate through all interactive elements.

Accessible Form

Live Region Example

Click the button to announce a message using a live region. This demonstrates how screen readers are notified of dynamic updates.

Resources

Want to learn more about web accessibility and semantic HTML? Check out these resources:

  • WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference (opens in new tab)
  • HTML Living Standard (opens in new tab)
  • A11y 101 (opens in new tab)

content.text:
`0.html` was already well built, so I didn't rewrite it. I made four small fixes to the form, mostly for screen readers. I haven't tested the changes in a browser or with a screen reader.

1. **The form's success message might not have been read out.** The status message was fully hidden while empty. Some screen readers ignore a message that appears in an area that was hidden that way. Now it stays in place with no margin until the message arrives.
2. **Repeated submits were silent.** Submitting the form a second time set the same text again, which screen readers usually don't announce. The script now clears the message and puts it back 100ms later so each submit is read out.
3. **The asterisk was never explained.** I added "Fields marked * are required." above the form. The asterisk is hidden from screen readers because the label already says "(required)" to them.
4. **Mistakes weren't highlighted.** The inputs now get a thicker red border when a value is invalid, using `:user-invalid`. That only kicks in after the user has interacted with the field, so the form doesn't show errors before they start typing.

I left the rest alone. The theming, focus styles, skip link, print styles and security settings are already solid. The `#top` link in the footer has no matching `id` on the page, but browsers scroll to the top for `#top` anyway, so it works.

result:
`0.html` was already well built, so I didn't rewrite it. I made four small fixes to the form, mostly for screen readers. I haven't tested the changes in a browser or with a screen reader.

1. **The form's success message might not have been read out.** The status message was fully hidden while empty. Some screen readers ignore a message that appears in an area that was hidden that way. Now it stays in place with no margin until the message arrives.
2. **Repeated submits were silent.** Submitting the form a second time set the same text again, which screen readers usually don't announce. The script now clears the message and puts it back 100ms later so each submit is read out.
3. **The asterisk was never explained.** I added "Fields marked * are required." above the form. The asterisk is hidden from screen readers because the label already says "(required)" to them.
4. **Mistakes weren't highlighted.** The inputs now get a thicker red border when a value is invalid, using `:user-invalid`. That only kicks in after the user has interacted with the field, so the form doesn't show errors before they start typing.

I left the rest alone. The theming, focus styles, skip link, print styles and security settings are already solid. The `#top` link in the footer has no matching `id` on the page, but browsers scroll to the top for `#top` anyway, so it works.
